key_insight: GOCP makes adaptive VQE simulation scalable by using greedy commutativity-based operator partitioning and fifth-order Taylor state evolution instead of explicit matrix exponentiation.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the classical bottleneck in sparse matrix scaling, enabling more efficient benchmarking and exploration of large variational ansatz growth for quantum chemistry problems.
method: Partition operators greedily by commutativity to streamline ansatz construction
Replace unitary exponentiation with chained O(5) Taylor series state updates
Use sparse matrix-vector operations under Jordan-Wigner and Bravyi-Kitaev mappings
evidence_signal: The abstract reports fidelity above 1 - 10^-6, sub-chemical accuracy for ground-state energies, and successful handling of operator manifolds larger than 2.68 x 10^8 elements.
watch_item: Accuracy and runtime gains may depend on sparsity, Taylor truncation stability, and problem-specific operator structure, so performance should be validated case by case.
paper_title: Alleviating the Sparse Matrix Scaling Bottleneck in Adaptive VQE via Greedy Operator Commutativity Partitioning and High-Order Taylor State Evolution
